messages:
monitor-bot: ALERT: p95 latency spike and throughput drop observed in prod-east-1 inference pool (gpu-pool-5). Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/east/runtime/inference

maria: seeing p95 jump from ~22ms -> ~180ms around 14:12 UTC, error rate small but throughput down ~40%. This is affecting web-tier requests.

aj: confirmed. GPU utilization ~85% but CPU on pgl nodes is pegged and context switches high. Throughput per-slot down.

dan: quick look at runtime logs — kernel-selector started returning `int8_fused_v2` for a subset of routes that expect fp16. There are fallback delays of ~120ms when mismatch occurs. Suspect selector heuristics flipped due to recent profile update.

sel: KV cache metrics show miss_rate jumped from 0.12 -> 0.74 and eviction_ratio 0.62. If cache thrashes, latency amplification + extra kernel warmups make sense. Could be noisy neighbor on pool-5 with larger batch sizes.

maria: tracing is weird — many requests stop emitting spans after `runtime.accept`. Dashboards show top traces missing spans for the spike window.

hao: update: tracing agent in prod-east restarted at 14:08 UTC due to config rollout. Sampling rules reverted to default 0.1, so many spans were dropped. That's why traces look incomplete.

aj: also noticed our dashboard panel uses 5m avg while the alert uses 1m. The alert fired later than raw metric spike — mismatch in aggregation windows made triage confusing.

dan: paste logs from node-27:
```
2026-03-17T14:12:03Z ERROR kernel_selector: selected kernel 'int8_fused_v2' incompatible with model 'gpt-small' -> fallback_delay=120ms
2026-03-17T14:12:03Z WARN kvcache: eviction_ratio=0.62 miss_rate=0.74
2026-03-17T14:12:04Z INFO batching: batch_size=32 chosen_by_heuristic, backlog=18
```

sel: that `batch_size=32` + `int8_fused` combo explains long tail. Batching heuristics favored larger batches after the recent change to prefer throughput; with kernel mismatch we pay huge cost per batch.

maria: I'm starting a live CPU + GPU pprof on the affected node: `curl -sS http://node-27:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > /tmp/profile-node27.pb` — will upload flamegraph.

sel: uploaded flamegraph gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/abc123 (note: many spans removed due to sampler). Logs also truncated because log-sampling was reduced last month.

aj: mitigation plan applied: rolled back kernel-selector profile to previous safe version (rolled at 14:20), reduced max_batch to 8 on gpu-pool-5, increased KV cache capacity for pool-5 nodes. Immediate latency improvement around 14:25.

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK: kernel-selector-profile -> v2026-03-10-rc (user: dan)

maria: post-rollback metrics: p95 back to ~28ms, throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline. However observability gaps remain — traces for the spike window are sparse and some logs are missing.

dan: action items we should track in the follow-up: 
- pin trace-sampling rules in deploy gating so agent restarts don't reset sampling to default
- add guard against kernel-selector profiles that change kernel family (e.g., int8 vs fp16) without canarying routes
- adjust dashboard panels to show consistent aggregation windows with alerts
- increase log-sampling for runtime for 24h after any selector/profile rollout

sel: agreed. Also need a short perf test that runs through kernel-selector permutations + batch sizes to catch regression patterns in CI.

hao: I'll own the tracing-sampling gate and do a fix to persist sampling rules across agent restarts.

maria: thanks all. I'll file an incident postmortem and include the pprof, flamegraphs, and the log excerpts. Observability gap is first-class item in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
